newsitem.title: PERU: Mudslide buries 150-200 people in Peru - authority.
newsitem.headline: Mudslide buries 150-200 people in Peru - authority.

text.p: A mudslide has buried about 40 houses containing 150 to 200 people in two villages in Peru's southeastern Andean region, local officials said on Tuesday.

"Two villages have totally disappeared. We're talking about 150 to 200 people buried," Luis Barra Pacheco, the mayor of Abancay, the capital of Peru's Apurimac department, told Reuters. He said seven bodies had been recovered so far.
Civil defence officials could not confirm the scale of the apparent disaster.
"We are trying to check right now how large it was," a civil defence spokesman told Reuters.
Barra said that heavy rains produced a massive flash flood at 4 a.m. (0900 GMT) Tuesday, burying the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra in the district of Tamburco near Abancay.
He said an estimated 300,000 cubic meters (10.5 million cubic feet) of mud slid off a nearby mountain. "It was a huge flash flood," he said. "The mountain buried two communities."
